societies.name: Warhammer 40,000 — Imperial servitor labor and AI restrictions
societies.society: The Imperial technological doctrine retaining human-derived servitor labor

scope.continuity: Imperial/Mechanicus doctrine as described through codex and prose lore
scope.period: Established Imperial production before any particular local collapse
scope.population: Living human and human-derived laboring subjects under servitor/AI doctrine
exclusions: Every servitor as unconscious non-person machinery
A uniform welfare charter across all Imperial planets
Pre-revolt Dark Age colonies
A separate duplicate point for forge-world servitor production

societies.description:
Imperial doctrine tolerates flesh-and-metal servitors while rejecting true artificial intelligence. Human beings, clones and other human-derived victims are remade to perform repetitive productive tasks that an independent thinking-machine system might otherwise undertake. This is retained as an interpretive zero variant: the constraint preserves human-derived labor despite the setting’s known technological alternatives. Fear and religious control, rather than protecting workers’ jobs, are the relevant motives. Useful labor is real and is not reclassified as meaningless simply because it is coerced.

Authority belongs to Imperial and Mechanicus elites, near the concentrated human-control position. Guarantees are weak for the scoped laboring subjects because their bodies, freedom and continued security can be forcibly withdrawn. Servitors’ surviving consciousness varies; some retain enough awareness or neural architecture to remain victims doing work, so they cannot all be removed from the denominator as machines. No reliable all-person participation rate is available. Forge-world production exemplifies the same doctrine here, while differing local planetary economies are not assigned a fabricated universal welfare constitution.

guarantees.basis: Forced conversion, bodily appropriation and unending servitude make security weak for the selected laboring subjects.

control.basis: Imperial/Mechanicus organic elites direct the restricted technology and labor forces; servitor operation is not AI sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: Variable consciousness and useful coerced work require a careful denominator; no all-person census exists.

evidence.claim: Tolerated human-derived servitors perform compulsory labor while true AI is rejected.
evidence.locator: Servitor overview/consciousness and Mechanicus labor-command sections

uncertainties: Interpretive zero variant: religious/security control, not demonstrated job protection.
Human-derived persons doing work remain visible.
Imperial local material institutions vary.
Forge-world servitor production is included in this doctrine scope.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Eclipse Phase — Titanian Commonwealth

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived citizens; other recognized persons are fellow participants
exclusions: Dormant ego files as active residents
Second-edition demographic/rule changes
All Autonomist Alliance polities as identical
AI bureaucrats as external sovereigns

societies.description:
Titan combines nanofabrication and a shared basic-needs economy with socially owned microcorps. Citizens do not buy mundane necessities through ordinary wages. Kroner instead allocate collective investment: the proceeds associated with productive activity are reinvested into social projects. This makes the distinction between access to life and the direction of additional resources explicit. Guarantees are strong, though citizenship, social-contract duties and the practical limits of available resources remain relevant.

Control lies well toward distributed ownership because the population’s Plurality directs common resources, microcorp funding and profits. Elected administrators and AI bureaucrats do not become an independent machine ruling class merely by carrying out those decisions. This is a human-and-recognized-person political community; active human-derived citizens are an explicit participation proxy and dormant files are excluded. Real research, care, defense and habitat construction continue, with contribution and reputation rewards. The record therefore leaves nonworking unresolved rather than treating currency-free basics or AI administration as proof that most people do no useful work. First-edition rules are kept separate from later revisions.

guarantees.basis: Shared mundane needs and fabrication are explicit, with social-contract/citizenship and resource limits.

control.basis: The Plurality directs socially owned microcorps, common resources and profits; delegates/AI administration remain constrained.

nonworking.basis: Social-money productivity, project work and reputation continue; no useful-work census is provided.

evidence.claim: Shared fabricated basics coexist with citizen-directed common microcorp investment.
evidence.locator: Titanian social organization, government and Commonwealth/Alliance explanation

uncertainties: First-edition scope; in-universe advocacy remains a source perspective.
Active human-derived proxy, with other recognized citizens acknowledged.
Basic access and investment currency are different mechanisms.
Contribution duties and useful work remain visible.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Eclipse Phase — Anarchist fabrication commons
societies.society: The first-edition anarchist habitat model within the Autonomist Alliance

scope.continuity: Eclipse Phase first-edition anarchist habitat description
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived residents in the described anarchist communes
exclusions: Titanian state institutions
Extropian private-property contracts
All outer-system settlements as identical
Dormant files or repeated avatars as more people

societies.description:
The described anarchist habitats combine equal cornucopia-machine access, common resources and robots doing most routine or demeaning tasks. Material basics can be obtained without ordinary wage purchases, while people organize useful services through voluntary collectives and councils. The guarantee estimate is strong but qualified: first-edition new-economy accounts retain citizenship or contribution criteria, bounded energy/material allowances and scarce living space or advanced bodies. These are not unlimited personal factories exempt from community obligations.

Production is governed through shared property and direct group decisions rather than a private machine owner or sovereign AI. That places control toward the distributed end of the map, while local variations and informal reputation pressure justify uncertainty. Automation does not remove care, maintenance, defense, art or administration as useful work. No all-person nonworking rate follows from the general delegation of routine jobs, so participation remains null. The record covers the anarchist institutional model, not every member of the broader Autonomist Alliance, and its active human-derived denominator excludes inactive backups and multiplied avatars.

guarantees.basis: Shared fabricated basics are explicit, but local eligibility/contribution rules, quotas and scarce resources qualify access.

control.basis: Common productive property, direct decisions and self-organized collectives establish more than public ownership in name.

nonworking.basis: Useful voluntary and contribution-based work continues; routine job delegation is not a census.

evidence.claim: Equal fabrication access and shared resources are maintained through direct collective organization with routine robot labor.
evidence.locator: Anarchists institutional description and new-economy allowance conditions

uncertainties: Anarchist model, not every outer-system polity.
Eligibility, contribution criteria and scarce resources remain explicit.
Active human-derived person proxy only.
No routine-task share is converted into nonworking.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Eclipse Phase — Inner-system transitional fabrication economy
societies.society: First-edition hypercorp-influenced habitats with public basic fabbers and private premium goods

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived eligible residents
exclusions: Every hypercorp site as the same old economy
Dormant infugees as already housed beneficiaries
Free access to every template, morph or spacecraft
All housing as unconditionally guaranteed

societies.description:
Inner-system transitional economies combine public basic fabbers with private control of more complex or fashionable goods. After a modest usage tax, residents can obtain food, ordinary clothing and furnishings without paying for each item, and basic medical care is generally supplied. This creates a real automatic material floor while preserving markets and inequality around designs, electronics, scarce materials, bodies and other privileges. The guarantee estimate is moderately strong for eligible residents, with housing and exclusion left as material limitations.

Corporate and governmental institutions retain important control over fabrication capabilities and restricted inputs. Public access to a limited machine menu does not establish equal ownership of the full productive infrastructure, so control remains near concentrated human authority. The record concerns the described transitional model rather than mislabeling every hypercorporate society as an old economy. Active human-derived citizens are a disclosed proxy; uninstantiated refugees are not automatically receiving bodily necessities. Design, research, maintenance and other useful work persists, and free basic output does not supply a participation census. Nonworking therefore stays unresolved.

guarantees.basis: Tax-qualified free basics and generally free basic care coexist with incomplete housing/morph access and restricted inputs.

control.basis: Public menus coexist with corporate/government control of important machines, templates and materials.

nonworking.basis: Free basics do not measure continuing design, maintenance, care or other useful activity.

evidence.claim: Public limited fabrication supplies basics after a usage tax alongside private premium production.

uncertainties: Transitional inner-system model, not every corporate economy.
Eligible active residents only; housing and body access are not invented.
Premium scarcity and basic provision are separated.
Participation remains unresolved.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Eclipse Phase — Jovian Republic’s restricted fabrication economy
societies.society: The first-edition old economy under the Jovian military junta

scope.population: Living human subjects and active human-derived persons where permitted
exclusions: All advanced machines as absent
All restricted technology as available to ordinary citizens
Other old-economy dictatorships as identical Jovian institutions
Hypothetical post-revolution provision

societies.description:
The Jovian Republic restricts ordinary access to nanofabrication while elites retain productive technology. In the old-economy model associated with its habitats, corporations or authorities sell goods that cornucopia machines can produce at very low cost. Residents still face hunger, homelessness and medical deprivation. The weak guarantee score therefore follows actual technological production combined with restrictive allocation, rather than assuming that conservatism means technology does not exist. Public access and private possession can be tightly policed.

Control is concentrated in the junta and protected institutional owners. Its bioconservative restrictions are relevant to the zero-variant theme, but the retained point describes a functioning machine-production economy whose output remains enclosed, not a second duplicate technological order. The population’s labor and payments remain important routes to necessities despite cheap fabrication. No nonworking percentage can be inferred from that inequality, and useful work remains real. Different Jovian habitats and other old-economy regimes need not share every detail; the record stays within the first-edition description and does not invent a later liberalized system.

guarantees.basis: Restricted fabrication, paid output and explicit deprivation undermine a universal material floor.

control.basis: Junta and privileged institutional owners control access and productive machines.

nonworking.basis: Technological exclusion and poverty are not an all-person useful-work census.

evidence.claim: The Jovian old-economy regime restricts public fabrication while controlled machines produce goods sold to residents.
evidence.locator: Jovian restrictions and The Old Economy section

uncertainties: Actual enclosed fabrication, not a claim that all advanced technology is absent.
No duplicate zero-variant point for the same material order.
First-edition scope and internal habitat variation are explicit.
Participation remains unresolved.

review_notes: Twelve ordered decisions yield five records, including one interpretive zero variant and one explicit producer-subset duplicate.
First-edition Eclipse Phase institutions are kept distinct from second-edition population or rule changes. Reproduced text and indexed primary excerpts are labeled.
New-economy citizenship/contribution conditions, finite quotas, scarce bodies and living space remain visible; free fabricated objects do not mean unlimited resources or no work.
The Jovian old economy really uses controlled fabrication, so its actual enclosed material order is retained once rather than duplicated solely for technological restrictions.
Imperial servitors retain variable human-derived consciousness and useful labor. Forge production is already within that doctrine scope.

Transhuman Space was not rescued through a complete book read. Real-world transhumanist policy, fan quests and incorrect nonbiological-clone wording were discarded; denied publisher access was respected.
